newsitem.title: USA: ECC wins outside support in proxy contest.
newsitem.headline: ECC wins outside support in proxy contest.

text.p: ECC International Corp said on Wednesday an independent shareholder advisory firm reaffirmed support for the company in a proxy fight with shareholder Michael Taglich.
On November 20, Michael Taglich, who owns 1,000 ECC shares, said he started a proxy contest with the company, recommending ECC hire an investment bank to sell the company or its businesses.
Taglich also proposed bylaw changes to allow shareholders owning 10 percent or more of the company's shares to call a special meeting at any time.
He also said then that ECC's recent bylaw changes were insincere because they could be changed by the board at any time and did not require sharesholder approval.
ECC had proposed allowing holders of 30 percent of the common stock to call special meetings. Taglich said this threshold was unreasonable.

On Wednesday, ECC said Institutional Shareholder Services, an independent shareholder advisory group, recommended shareholders vote for the company's proposals and against Taglich's at its December 3 annual shareholder meeting.
ECC said the group's backing was based on a review of proxy materials and discussions with Taglich.
The group said Taglich's proposal to hire an investment banker was too narrowly focuesd, and that the 30 percent ownership threshold was substantially less than required by many other companies.
